newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE CRUSH SCOTLAND FOR HISTORIC GRAND SLAM.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE CRUSH SCOTLAND FOR HISTORIC GRAND SLAM.

text.p: France clinched their first grand slam at home on Saturday by crushing Scotland 47-20 in their last Five Nations' match at Parc des Princes.
France, whose previous four clean sweeps in the tournament were completed on foreign territory, scored two tries in each half.
But the key to their comfortable victory was accurate goalkicking by centre Christophe Lamaison, who succeeded in all but one of his 10 attempts to score 24 points.
The win was particularly sweet for the French, who had been waiting for a grand slam for 10 years and were looking forward to an exciting conclusion to 24 years of adventure at Parc des Princes.
From next year, France, whose previous grand slams were in 1968, 1977, 1981 and 1987, will entertain their guests at the new Stade de France currently being built in the Paris suburb of St Denis.
The players received a standing ovation from the emotional crowd of 47,000 as they embarked on a lap of honour after outclassing a brave but limited Scottish side.
France moved ahead with a penalty by Lamaison after two minutes but Scotland's fullback Rowen Shepherd responded five minutes later to level the tie.
Lamaison then slotted two more penalties before captain Abdel Benazzi charged for France's first try in the 25th minute, which Lamaison converted to put the home team 16-3 up.

After three more points from Shepherd, the French treated their fans with a brilliant move sparked by fullback Jean-Luc Sadourny which led to a Laurent Leflamand try converted by Lamaison in the 31st minute.
A drop goal by Sadourny saw France increase their lead to 26-6 before Scotland responded with a try between the posts by centre Alan Tait and a Shepherd conversion.
The teams changed ends with France leading 26-13 and an unstoppable Lamaison soon made it 32-13 with two penalties in the first five minutes of the second half.
The powerful Tait breached the French defence once again for his second try converted by Shepherd and Scotland trailed32-20 with 30 minutes remaining.
The visitors lost fly-half Graig Chalmers, who left the pitch on a stretcher after a nasty tackle, and rest of the match was a one-sided affair.
"It was catch-up rugby from the start," said Scotland coach Richie Dixon. "The players surrendered from the kick-off and there was very little they could do."
A penalty by Lamaison followed by a try by prop Franck Tournaire converted by Lamaison put the issue beyond doubt.

Cheered on by their fans singing the French anthem, La Marseillaise, the French decided to add a touch of Gallic finesse with a classic move in which all the backs touched the ball for a try by Olivier Magne eight minutes from time.
Perhaps feeling he had done enough, Lamaison missed the conversion. All the French substitutes then came in to savour the atmosphere.
"It was magic," said winger David Venditti. "I have never experienced something so strong in my life."
Lamaison said he did not want to leave the pitch. "It was such a great feeling, I just wanted to stay there," he said.
Although France have lost several key players through injury since the start of the tournament, they have beaten Ireland and Wales before upsetting England 23-20 at Twickenham.
"I liked the spirit of the team today but we must continue to work," said French coach Jean-Claude Skrela, already anticipating the tour of Australia in June.
Teams:

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Laurent Leflamand (17-Pierre Bondouy 74th), 13-Christophe Lamaison, 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Venditti (16-Ugo Mola 74th); 10-David Aucagne, 9-Guy Accoceberry (18-Philippe Carbonneau 76th); 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Olivier Magne, 6-Abdelatif Benazzi (captain), 5-Hugues Miorin (19-Richard Castel 49th), 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Franck Tournaire (20-Jean-Louis Jordana 72nd), 2-Marc Dal Maso (21-Marc de Rougemont 73rd), 1-Didier Casadei.

Scotland - 15-Rowen Shepherd; 14-Tony Stanger, 13-Alan Tait (16-Cameron Glasgow 62nd), 12-Gregor Townsend, 11-Kenny Logan; 10-Craig Chalmers (17-Duncan Hodge 51st), 9-Bryan Redpath; 8-Peter Walton (19-Doddie Weir 21st), 7-Ian Smith, 6-Rob Wainwright (captain), 5-Andy Reed, 4-Doddie Weir, 3-Mattie Stewart, 2-Graham Ellis, 1-Tom Smith.
